trial_court: 1st Additional Distrct Judge,Shujalpur, Distt. Shajapur in Case No. 06/2019(HMA)
case_name: Chetan Sahgal vs Smt. Richa Sahgarl Sahgal
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Appellant and respondent got married on 12.05.2009 as per Hindu rights and customs. The respondent never lived at her matrimonial house and have not cohabited.

legal_principles.principle: The admissibility of additional evidence does not depend upon the relevancy to the issue on hand, or on the fact whether the applicant had an opportunity for adducing such evidence at an earlier stage or not.
legal_principles.held: As observed and held by this Court in the case of A. Andisamy Chettiar v. A. Subburaj Chettiar, reported in (2015) 17 SCC 713, the admissibility of additional evidence does not depend upon the relevancy to the issue on hand, or on the fact whether the applicant had an opportunity for adducing such evidence at an earlier stage or not.
cited_cases: A. Andisamy Chettiar v. A. Subburaj Chettiar, (2015) 17 SCC 713

legal_principles.principle: The appellate court may permit additional evidence if the conditions laid down in Rule are found to exist and the parties are not entitled, as of right, to the admission of such evidence.
legal_principles.held: However, at the same time, where the additional evidence sought to be adduced removes the cloud of doubt over the case and the evidence has a direct and important bearing on the main issue in the suit and interest of justice clearly renders it imperative that it may be allowed to be permitted on record, such application may be allowed.
cited_cases: Sanjay Kumar Singh V State Of Jharkhand, (2022) LiveLaw (SC) 268

outcome.final_order: The present appeal has been filed by the appellant (husband) being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 01.07.2019 passed by the trial court.
